W_LIST26.title: IDI: women in the 2026 electoral lists
W_LIST26.note: List presence supports access to candidacy only. Poll-dependent percentages are not scored and do not establish quota rules. Joint-list figures are not assigned to component parties.

W_RULES26.title: IDI: candidate-selection rules for 2026
W_RULES26.note: Current election review: Likud guarantees named places; Democrats alternate women and men. Used for party rules, not a universal statutory obligation.

W_HAREDI.title: IDI: Haredi local elections and exclusion of women
W_HAREDI.note: 2024 review reproduces Shas and UTJ’s older explanation of sex-specific political roles. Read with the 2026 lists; not a blanket description of all Haredi people or parties.

W_BEYAHAD.title: Beyahad: programme on the status of women
W_BEYAHAD.note: Official live plan. Distinguishes party-funding incentives from a 50% target for senior public-service posts.

W_DEMOCRATS.title: Democrats: five-point vision, July 2025
W_DEMOCRATS.note: Pages 3 and 7: active inclusion and equal rights. Opposition to exclusion does not specify every voluntary-separation arrangement.

W_HADASH.title: Hadash: current bilingual principles and candidates
W_HADASH.note: Arabic and Hebrew principles explicitly support women’s equality; its own candidates include women. No Joint List attribution.

W_OTZMA26.title: Arutz 7: Son Har-Melech on separate academic tracks
W_OTZMA26.note: Attributable statement supporting optional separate tracks. Does not establish every equality safeguard or a general position against women’s employment.

W_COALITION23.title: Law professors’ forum: gender separation provisions in coalition agreements
W_COALITION23.note: Historical analysis hosted by the Knesset; indexed text names Shas, UTJ and Religious Zionism separately. Direct PDF retrieval failed. Current continuity is explicitly an inference.

W_EXCLUSION26.title: Israel Women’s Network: exclusion of women from public life
W_EXCLUSION26.note: Advocacy organization’s submission to the Knesset committee, page 1: explicitly identifies ideological exclusion in Shas and UTJ. Used for party practice, not its separate legal assessment. Printed numeric and Hebrew dates are inconsistent; year only.

limitations: Q21 compares a party’s own candidacy rules and practice, not an inferred view on forcing all other parties to adopt the same rule. Named exclusions distinguish an ideological bar from an accidental all-male list.

A quota at specific list positions can be weaker than the respondent’s preferred minimum. The coarse quota component captures the mechanism and does not assert a particular percentage. List percentages alone are never converted into quota or parity commitments.
Q22 separates active or formal equality policies from gender-separated provision. Support for separate provision does not mean opposition to women working, studying or holding every leadership role.

Broad permission for separation does not establish consent safeguards, compulsory separation, or every detail in a respondent’s answer. Historical coalition commitments remain historical; continuity inferences are visible and discounted.

No values are assigned from a party’s religious or secular identity alone. Several parties and components remain unknown. Short runs include one or two questions from this category, never a hidden category multiplier.

Arabic sources were reviewed for Hadash and Balad. Joint-list totals are not transferred to Ta’al, Balad or Hadash. Old Balad programme text remains historical with separately discounted continuity estimates.

Q22’s community-autonomy answer explicitly includes male-only political leadership and public representation within the community. This does not assert a ban on every managerial role. Evidence about separate services scores only the separation component; it does not establish support for this leadership restriction or fill an unknown equality_policy component.
